result.summary: This diff adds cursor position (CPR) reporting, cancellation-based shutdown of the event loop with retry/backoff, a signal-safe SIGWINCH self-pipe with a C API for resize callbacks, and Windows win32-input-mode handling, plus mechanical updates for Zig 0.17 builtins (@backingInt/@fromBackingInt, field_names). I checked the build script, the dependency manifest, the tty/signal code, the PTY exec path and the tests: nothing sends data off the machine, reads secrets, downloads code or hides behaviour. The only notable item is the zigimg dependency moving to a hash-pinned third-party fork.

findings.title: Image dependency switched from upstream zigimg to a third-party fork
findings.detail: The zigimg dependency moves from github.com/zigimg/zigimg to a personal fork, github.com/sergot/zigimg, at a new commit. The content hash is pinned, and minimum_zig_version rises to 0.17.0 at the same time. That pattern points to a fork made for compatibility with the new compiler while upstream catches up. Still, it moves a transitive dependency to a different publisher. The fork's code is a separate review unit and is not judged here.

findings.title: SIGWINCH self-pipe and dispatch thread
findings.detail: SIGWINCH handling now only writes a byte to a non-blocking self-pipe, which is async-signal-safe. A concurrent task reads the pipe and runs the registered callbacks. New C API functions tty_notify_winsize and tty_remove_winsize_notify expose up to 8 callbacks. This is ordinary terminal-library behaviour.

findings.title: Event loop shutdown and retry rework
findings.detail: The input loop stops by closing the queue and cancelling the task instead of sending a device status report. Transient read errors are retried with capped backoff, and malformed input is discarded. These are robustness changes with no external effects.

findings.title: Build changes limited to tests and examples
findings.detail: The build adds a translate-c step for include/vaxis.h, used only by the ABI conformance test, and a C example test executable (examples/c/tty.c) attached to the test step. Neither affects the library artifacts consumers link.

data_flows.what: Cursor position request escape sequence (CSI 6n) written by the new queryCursorPosition; the terminal's reply is parsed back as a cursor_position event.
Win32-input-mode enable/disable sequences (ESC[?9001h on init, ESC[?9001l on deinit) so key releases and modifiers arrive as input records.
A single zero byte written from the SIGWINCH handler to wake a dispatch thread that runs resize callbacks. The pipe is created with CLOEXEC and never leaves the process.
data_flows.to: an internal self-pipe within the same process
